name: Metal Support
description: The Metal backend's Linux-safe parts (Sources/CoreRender/Metal): binary16 half-float conversion for filling rgba16Float textures from Float32 buffers and reading them back; MetalCapabilities, the proven op set and health state that RenderDispatcher reads; SurfaceTiling, the 256 px tile grid a surface's textures follow, on CoreRaster's shared tile math, with the tiles a rect touches and the default memory budget (half the working set, at least one tile); PipelineKey, the identity of one cached compute pipeline (op family plus a short identifier variant) and the kernel function name it maps to; and DisplayTable, CoreColor's DisplayTransfer byte rules as Float thresholds (the curve's and the alpha's, plus the linear sRGB to Display P3 matrix as Float) that the Metal display kernel uploads, with encode, the kernel's per-pixel rule in Swift. Pure Swift bit, integer and string math, no Metal import, so it builds, tests and mutates on Linux.
